notes: Frame narration is in the present; Cynyr's tale carries the target (roedd for background, -odd/daeth/es i/des i/clywais i for events).

The noun arfer (hen arfer, s-label arfer1) and the pattern roedd … yn arfer + VN (ro'n i'n arfer cario; roedd y bardd yn arfer chwarae) are kept in separate sentences, each with its own gloss, as the plan note asks.

Lexicon delta lists the imperfect paradigm forms under cy-bod (roedd, oedd, doedd, ro'n i, o'n i, ro't ti, ro'n ni, ro'ch chi, ro'n nhw) so the cards and the coverage checker see them as forms, plus a pattern-arfer card stage on cy-arfer.

Invented continuity (flagged for the Pennod 30 writer): Elen was a maid (morwyn) to Uthr's young queen at Caerllion; Cynyr carried the king's sword and once dropped it on the bard's foot; an old wizard with a tall black hat served at Uthr's court (the children cry 'Myrddin!'; Cynyr does not confirm).
Arth falls asleep before the baby is mentioned and does not hear it; Mali alone is left asking 'Ble mae'r babi nawr?' (Mali suspects from 17).
Myrddin's arrival at the real door in the snow, just as the tale reaches the knock, is the turn; Cynyr stops and Elen ends the evening with 'Mae hi'n hwyr.'

Checker warning justified: prior coverage is about 84% (Rhan 2 floor 88%) because the imperfect paradigm itself (roedd, oedd, doedd, ro'n i, ro't ti, ro'n ni, ro'ch chi, o'n i) is new here and supplies 74 of about 1,150 tokens; without the target forms prior coverage is about 90%. Every one is the chapter's taught pattern in a story sentence, not an opaque word.

Fluent review 2026-10-12 applied: B.b7 prompt now serves the food ('yn rhoi … ar y bwrdd') instead of 'gwneud'; C.c1, C.c2 and C.c4 answer keys widened. Review-question verdicts, all accepted unchanged: s016 'Stori am yr amser pan o'n i'n ifanc'; s035 'pan gwympodd' (SM after pan); s059 'Ro'n i'n forwyn i'r frenhines'; s067 'ac ro'n i' (ac before roedd and its contractions); s092 'Pwy oedd y babi?'; s008 noun 'arfer' (custom); s017 'Mae'r gwynt yn curo ar y drws'; s039 keep 'dig' (valid standard informal; grac not needed).

Recall pass 2026-10-18: recurrences woven into Cynyr's tale and the frame — cy-olwyn / cy-botwm (s134, Pero sleeps with Myrddin's little wheel and big button from Pennod 15), cy-clymu (s020), cy-pedwar (s021), cy-prynu (s026, Cai), cy-mochyn (s028), cy-ugain (s029) and cy-cyfrif (new s132, Mali checks the number; s030 now opens with Cynyr's 'Do'), cy-saith (s046), cy-ph-ar-goll (s083–s084), cy-heibio-i (s085), cy-disgyn (s086), cy-gwlan (s087), cy-ysgafn (s088), cy-drych and cy-pwll (new s133, Mali links the mirror and the pool to the baby). s006 split (s006 + s134) to keep sentence length ≤ 22. Also cy-anghofio (s127, Mali never forgets).
Critique pass 2026-10-18: s007, s023, s070, s113 reverted to HEAD (milk source, price, storm duration, snack packaging were unmotivated); s135 retired with the s007 revert.

Audit-fix pass 2026-10-19: Cai's 'Dw i ddim yn ofni taranau!' (s068) moved after s074 ('roedd e'n ofni'r taranau'), so taranau is first met in the storm description with its gloss (s072) and Cai's boast answers Pero's fear. s134 Pero sleeps with Myrddin's wheel only (in Pennod 15 the button stayed on the table). s126 cyfrinach glossed from the known cyfrinachol. Pensa A.a6–a8 accept full answers (Oedd. Roedd e'n …; Do. Daeth e …).

grammar.nodyn_en: Roedd/oedd is the imperfect of bod: it paints the background (Roedd storm fawr 'There was a big storm'). The -odd/daeth past tells what happened (pan ddaeth Myrddin 'when Myrddin came'). Questions: Oedd …? — Oedd / Nac oedd, not Do / Naddo. Ro'n i'n arfer + verb-noun = 'I used to'. Pan causes soft mutation.
